texto: 1. **Regla de alternancia**: If the subject does the action on himself without another object, the reflexive goes in Accusative: **Ich wasche mich** (I wash). But if a direct object (usually parts of the body, clothing or ideas) appears, the reflexive becomes Dativo: **Ich wasche mir (Dativ) die Hände (Akkusativ)**.

2. **Formas afectadas**: Only the first and second person of the singular change: **ich → mir**, **du → dir**. The third person of the singular and plural remains unchanged: **er/sie/es/sie/Sie → sich**; and the first / second person of the plural: **wir → uns**, **ihr → euch**.

3. **Verbos reflexivos mentales con Dativo**: They are very common in German: **sich etwas überlegen** (think about something): **Ich überlege mir einen Plan**; **sich etwas merken** (memorize something): **Ich merke mir die Nummer**; **sich etwas vorstellen** (imagine something): **Ich kann mir das vorstellen**.

bloques.pregunta: Why is «mir» and not «mich» used in «Ich wasche mir die Hände»?

opciones.texto: Porque la presencia del objeto directo «die Hände» desplaza al pronombre reflexivo al dativo
opciones.explicacion: As there is already an accusative complement («die Hände»), the beneficiary person is moved to a dative.

opciones.texto: Porque «die Hände» es un sustantivo plural y los plurales exigen dativo
opciones.explicacion: The number of the object does not alter the rule of distribution of cases between patient and beneficiary.

opciones.texto: Because «waschen» is an intransitive verb that rejects the accuser
opciones.explicacion: «waschen» is transitory and rules accusative for the direct object washed.

bloques.pregunta: What forms of reflexive pronoun differentiate between Accurative and Dative?

opciones.texto: Únicamente la primera y segunda persona del singular: mich/mir y dich/dir
opciones.explicacion: The «sich», «uns» and «euch» forms are identical in both accusative and dative.

opciones.texto: All grammatical people without exception have different forms
opciones.explicacion: In 3rd person («sich») and in plural («uns», «euch») the forms do not change.

opciones.texto: Only the third person of the plural has an exclusive form for the purpose of teaching.
opciones.explicacion: The third person always uses «sich» regardless of the case.

bloques.frase: Ich putze ___ jeden Morgen gründlich die Zähne.

opciones.explicacion: The direct object is «die Zähne» (accusative), so the first person's reflexive must be «mir» (dative).
«mich» would be used if there was no object («Ich wasche mich»), but here it would cause double accusation.
It is the second person («t»), incompatible with the «ich» subject.

bloques.frase: Hast du ___ diese wichtige Telefonnummer gemerkt?

opciones.explicacion: With the direct object «diese Telefonnummer» (accusative), the reflexive with «du» must be «dir» (dative).
It would be accusative, wrong in the presence of an express direct object.
It would refer to the first person («to me»), not the person questioned («du»).

bloques.frase: Ich kann mir den großen Erfolg schon genau vorstellen.

opciones.texto: That I can already conceive and clearly imagine the great future success.
opciones.explicacion: «sich etwas vorstellen» with dativa means to be mentally represented or to imagine something.

opciones.texto: What a rejection of success because I'm afraid to work hard.
opciones.explicacion: It contrasts the meaning of the phrase.

opciones.texto: That I didn't succeed in yesterday's job interview.
opciones.explicacion: It speaks of conceive of future success, not of past failure.

bloques.frase: Er zieht ___ vor dem Vorstellungsgespräch einen warmen Mantel an.

opciones.explicacion: The third person reflexive of the singular («er») is «sich», both in both accusative and dative.
«ihm» is a personal pronoun of a non-reflective indirect object (it would put it to another person).
It is the personal pronoun masculine in accusative, not a reflexive form.

bloques.frase: Ich ziehe mir die Anzugjacke an
bloques.explicacion: subject + verb + dative mir + object + particle an at the end.

intro: When a reflexive action also has an explicit direct accentuative complement, the reflexive pronoun of the first and second person must be passed to the didative.
